body.description:
The midrise portion of 301 Mission Street has five below-grade parking levels. Water has been leaking through of the exterior perimeter walls of the below-grade garage.  Previous efforts to repair the leaks have met with limited success. Off gassing of ammonia in two contained areas in the B5 level of the parking garage has been measured between 18 and 22 ppm. The proposed testing will attempt to determine the source of the off gassing, and examine the effectiveness of the previous waterproofing efforts and concrete materials used to construct the below grade garage. 

Work will consist of taking six 6” core samples of the exterior garage walls, two at level B4 and four at level B5.  Test cores will be examined by experts to determine the effectiveness of waterproofing materials used in the shotcrete mix and repairs. The experts will then make recommendations for waterproofing repairs, methods, and materials for a long-term solution to the leaking problem. Mockups will then be done in limited areas to test the effectiveness of the material recommended.  After completion of the waterproofing mockups, additional cores will be taken.  Results from this second round of coring will be evaluated to determine the effectiveness of the proposed long-term solution. Building permit applications will be submitted to DBI for both the waterproofing mockups and subsequent coring prior to commencement of the work.

The proposed scope of work consists of drilling a single rotary-wash boring that will be converted to a monitoring well in the sidewalk of Fremont Street near Millennium Tower (301 Mission Street). The boring will be drilled to a depth of about 170 feet below ground surface under the observation of a field engineer. The field engineer will determine the depth, sampler type, and frequency of sample collection during drilling based on data collected by previous geotechnical investigations at the site and observed conditions during drilling. After drilling the boring, the boring will be converted to a monitoring well. The driller will flush the borehole with biodegradable drilling mud and attach the VW piezometers to a sacrificial PVC pipe at the desired intervals. The driller will backfill the boring with a grout mix under the observation of the San Francisco Dept. of Public Health and San Francisco Public Works. After installing the VW piezometers and grouting the borehole, the new monitoring well will be covered by a monitoring well cover. Soil cuttings from the boring will be stored in 55-gallon steel drums and transported off-site for characterization and disposal by the driller. The purpose of the project is to gather data to measure soil compressibility.
